summary: Scholze proves that the Hecke eigensystems in the torsion cohomology H^i(X_K, ℳ_ξ/p^m) of the locally symmetric spaces of GL_n over a totally real or CM field F carry Galois determinants: there is a nilpotent ideal I with I^N = 0, N depending only on [F:ℚ] and n, such that the Hecke image 𝕋(K, ξ, i, m)/I receives an n-dimensional continuous determinant of G_{F,S} with the Hecke polynomials as Frobenius characteristic polynomials (Theorem 5.4.1). Consequences: mod p Galois representations for all such Hecke eigensystems (Theorem 1.0.3 = Corollary 5.4.3), Hecke-algebra-valued representations at non-Eisenstein ideals (Corollary 5.4.4, Calegari–Geraghty's Conjecture B up to a nilpotent ideal) and a new proof of the Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne theorem (Corollary 5.4.2). The totally real case assumes Arthur's classification; Remark 5.4.6 gives the unconditional range (F CM containing an imaginary quadratic field, S pulled back from ℚ). The route: a perfectoid Hebbarkeitssatz and Zariski closed embeddings of perfectoid spaces (§2); the perfectoid Siegel space at infinite level, built from canonical subgroups, Frobenius lifts and Tate traces on the anticanonical tower, and its Hodge–Tate period map with ω ≅ π_HT*ω_Fl (§3); the same for Hodge type, the identification of compactly supported completed cohomology with the cohomology of p-adic cusp forms at infinite level, vanishing above the middle degree, and p-adic interpolation of completed-cohomology eigensystems by classical cusp forms (§4); and, in §5, the Galois determinants of classical cusp forms on Sp_{2n}/U(n,n) (Arthur, Mok, the regular algebraic conjugate self-dual case), transfer to the boundary of the Borel–Serre compactification, whose Levi is Res GL_n, and a twisting argument that separates the n-dimensional factor. The atlas already plans almost all of it: the campaign roadmap TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure (TC.0–TC.4) takes this paper as its organizing source, with PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S0–S3, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0–T4, PerfectoidSpaces P4/P7/P8 (whose packets cite the paper node by node), PerfectoidQuotients Q4, AdicSpacesPartII R2/R3, CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.7/CC.8 (decomposition nodes on Theorem 4.2.1 and Corollaries 4.2.2–4.2.3), ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.4, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0–IHG.5, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2–AG2.4, EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4. Three inputs are missing and are routed as sources of existing layers: Illusie's deformation theory of flat commutative group schemes (Theorem 3.2.1, to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.6); the Siegel Hasse invariant, its ordinarity criterion and boundary behaviour, and the lifting lemma for canonical subgroups (to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T3); and the holomorphic discrete series of Sp_{2n}(ℝ) and U(n,n) with the cusp-form dictionary (to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4/AF.5). Nothing in the Mathlib or Tau Ceti baselines covers any item. Eleven source issues are recorded, five of them already found by atlas packets.

items.name: Conjecture 1.0.1: the global Langlands correspondence for GL_n in its L-algebraic form
items.statement: Let F be a number field, p a rational prime, and fix an isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p. Then for any n ≥ 1 there is a unique bijection between (i) the set of L-algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n(𝔸_F), and (ii) the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible continuous representations Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) which are almost everywhere unramified and de Rham at the places dividing p, such that the bijection matches Satake parameters with eigenvalues of Frobenius elements.
items.note: A conjecture, not proved in the paper; it motivates Conjecture 1.0.2 and Theorems 1.0.3–1.0.4. ML.0 registers endpoints with an explicit conjectural status and ML.5 formalizes the statements of the general global correspondence; the notion of L-algebraic (Buzzard–Gee) is AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4.

items.name: Completed cohomology and its torsion-level and compactly supported versions
items.statement: For a Shimura variety (S_K)_K of Hodge type and a tame level K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p), the compactly supported completed cohomology is H̃^i_{c,K^p} = lim_m colim_{K_p} H^i_c(S_{K_pK^p}, ℤ/p^mℤ). For a reductive group G with locally symmetric spaces X_K, H̃^i_{K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ) = colim_{K_p} H^i(X_{K_pK^p}, ℤ/p^nℤ) and H̃^i_{K^p}(ℤ_p) = lim_n H̃^i_{K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ) (Calegari–Emerton); in §4.2, for (G, D) of Hodge type with a fixed embedding into (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}) and K^p inside the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p, H̃^i_{c,K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ) = colim_{K_p} H^i_c(X_{K_pK^p}, ℤ/p^nℤ). These carry actions of G(ℚ_p) and of the Hecke operators away from p.
items.note: CC.1–CC.2 build the torsion colimit and the completed inverse limit; the CC.8 decomposition node scholze-4-2-convention-and-the-perfectoid-comparison records exactly the §4.2 convention (compact support, torsion coefficients, tame level in the level-N subgroup).

items.name: Theorem 1.0.3 with Conjecture 1.0.2: Galois representations for mod p Hecke eigensystems of GL_n over totally real and CM fields
items.statement: Let F be a number field and X_K, K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}), the locally symmetric spaces for GL_n/F. Conjecture 1.0.2: for any system of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in H^i(X_K, 𝔽_p) there is a continuous semisimple representation Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(𝔽̄_p) such that the eigenvalues of Frobenius and the Hecke eigenvalues match up. Theorem 1.0.3: Conjecture 1.0.2 holds if F is CM and contains an imaginary-quadratic field. Assuming the work of Arthur [Arthur's endoscopic classification], it holds if F is totally real or CM.
items.note: The precise forms are Corollary 5.4.3 (with coefficients ℳ_{ξ,K}) and Remark 5.4.6 (the unconditional range). As in the accepted extractions PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/69 and /72, PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23/thm-2-1-24 and PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-24/2, the torsion determinant is planned by TC.2–TC.4 with IHG.5's nilpotent descent and IHG.1's reconstruction over a field. The totally real (symplectic) branch keeps Arthur's classification as a hypothesis, registered by ML.4; the CM branch uses the unitary trace comparison of ET.7a (Shin's results).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.1, first part: the formal model glued from an affinoid cover with compatible sections
items.statement: Let K be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with ring of integers 𝒪_K and a nonzero topologically nilpotent ϖ ∈ 𝒪_K. Let 𝒳 be a reduced proper rigid-analytic variety over K, considered as an adic space, ℒ a line bundle on 𝒳, and 𝒳 = ⋃_{i∈I} 𝒰_i a cover by finitely many affinoid opens 𝒰_i = Spa(R_i, R_i^+), R_i^+ = R_i° the power-bounded elements; for J ⊂ I let 𝒰_J = ⋂_{i∈J} 𝒰_i = Spa(R_J, R_J^+). Assume sections s_j^{(i)} ∈ H^0(𝒰_i, ℒ), j ∈ I, such that (i) for all i, s_i^{(i)} is invertible and s_j^{(i)}/s_i^{(i)} ∈ H^0(𝒰_i, 𝒪_𝒳^+); (ii) for all i, j, 𝒰_{ij} ⊂ 𝒰_i is defined by |s_j^{(i)}/s_i^{(i)}| = 1; (iii) for all i_1, i_2, j, |s_j^{(i_1)}/s_{i_1}^{(i_1)} − s_j^{(i_2)}/s_{i_1}^{(i_1)}| ≤ |ϖ| on 𝒰_{i_1i_2}. Then for J ⊂ J′ the map Spf R_{J′}^+ → Spf R_J^+ is an open embedding of formal schemes, formally of finite type; gluing them defines a formal scheme 𝔛 over 𝒪_K with an open cover by 𝔘_i = Spf R_i^+ and 𝔘_J = ⋂_{i∈J} 𝔘_i = Spf R_J^+, whose generic fibre is 𝒳.
items.note: TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure's source contract assigns §2.1 ('gluing compatible formal models from admissible affinoid covers and model comparison') to AdicSpacesPartII; R2 constructs admissible formal schemes, their generic fibres and models of affinoids, and TC.0 compares the integral structure sheaves of formal models with power-bounded affinoid sections on the specified covers. Proof: Bosch–Lütkebohmert, Formal and rigid geometry I, Lemma 1.2(c) and Proposition 1.3.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.1, second part: the integral line bundle, its reductions of sections, projectivity and ampleness
items.statement: Let K be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with ring of integers 𝒪_K and a nonzero topologically nilpotent ϖ ∈ 𝒪_K. In the situation of Lemma 2.1.1 there is a unique invertible sheaf 𝔏 on 𝔛 with generic fibre ℒ such that s_j^{(i)} ∈ H^0(𝔘_i, 𝔏) ⊂ H^0(𝒰_i, ℒ) = H^0(𝔘_i, 𝔏)[ϖ^{-1}], with s_i^{(i)} an invertible section. There are unique sections s̄_j ∈ H^0(𝔛, 𝔏/ϖ) with s̄_j = s_j^{(i)} mod ϖ in H^0(𝔘_i, 𝔏/ϖ) for all i ∈ I. Furthermore 𝔛 is projective and 𝔏 is ample.
items.note: Used in §4.3 (proof of Theorem 4.3.1) to build the formal model 𝔛*_{K_pK^p} with the ample integral bundle ω^int.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.2: the integral model of a coherent ideal sheaf
items.statement: Let K be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with ring of integers 𝒪_K and a nonzero topologically nilpotent ϖ ∈ 𝒪_K. In the situation of Lemma 2.1.1, let ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_𝒳 be a coherent ideal sheaf. Then the association 𝔘_i ↦ H^0(𝒰_i, ℐ ∩ 𝒪_𝒳^+) extends uniquely to a coherent 𝒪_𝔛-module 𝔍 with generic fibre ℐ.
items.note: TC.0 establishes the ideal-of-boundary sheaves and their integral models; R3 supplies coherent ideals on the generic fibre.

items.name: Definition 2.2.1: Zariski closed subsets of an affinoid perfectoid space
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. A subset Z ⊂ |𝒳| is Zariski closed if there is an ideal I ⊂ R such that Z = {x ∈ 𝒳 : |f(x)| = 0 for all f ∈ I}.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P4 packet node zariski-closed-immersion (from this definition) and P8 node zariski-closed-embedding.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.2: the universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. Assume Z ⊂ 𝒳 is Zariski closed. There is a universal perfectoid space 𝒵 over K with a map 𝒵 → 𝒳 for which |𝒵| → |𝒳| factors over Z. The space 𝒵 = Spa(S, S^+) is affinoid perfectoid, the map R → S has dense image, and |𝒵| → Z is a homeomorphism.
items.note: P4 node universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed; P8 node limit-of-zariski-closed-embeddings. By Remark 2.2.4 as corrected (item below) R → S is in fact surjective. 𝒵 = 𝒳 ×_{Z} is identified with Z, and 𝒵 → 𝒳 is called a (Zariski) closed embedding.

items.name: Remark 2.2.3: the universal property of the Zariski closed perfectoid subspace for bounded targets
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. In Lemma 2.2.2, for any affinoid K-algebra (T, T^+) with T^+ ⊂ T bounded and any map (R, R^+) → (T, T^+) for which Spa(T, T^+) → Spa(R, R^+) factors over Z, there is a unique factorization (R, R^+) → (S, S^+) → (T, T^+).
items.note: P4 node universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed cites this remark.

items.name: Remark 2.2.4 as corrected: R → S is surjective for a Zariski closed subset
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. For Z ⊂ 𝒳 Zariski closed and 𝒵 = Spa(S, S^+) as in Lemma 2.2.2, the map R → S is surjective, and 𝒵 → 𝒳 is strongly Zariski closed in the corrected sense of Definition 2.2.6. The printed remark asserts the opposite (see sourceIssues E1).
items.note: Corrected statement: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5; Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Theorem 5.8. PerfectoidQuotients Q4 proves exactly this. Nothing later in the paper uses the printed caution.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.5: closed embeddings in characteristic p are strongly Zariski closed
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. Assume K has characteristic p and 𝒵 = Spa(S, S^+) → 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) is a (Zariski) closed embedding. Then R^+ → S^+ is almost surjective; in particular R → S is surjective.
items.note: The characteristic-p case of Q4's theorem; the proof constructs the perfectoid quotient R°a/(ϖ, f, f^{1/p}, …) directly.

items.name: Definition 2.2.6 as corrected: strongly Zariski closed maps
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. A map 𝒵 = Spa(S, S^+) → 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) of affinoid perfectoid spaces over K is strongly Zariski closed if R^+ → S^+ is almost surjective and S^+ is the integral closure in S of the image of R^+. Such a map is Zariski closed, defined by the ideal I = ker(R → S). (The printed definition omits the plus-ring condition; see sourceIssues E2.)
items.locator: §2.2, Definition 2.2.6 and the sentence after it, p. 957
items.note: P4 nodes strongly-zariski-closed-criterion and strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed; the corrected form is Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Definition 5.7(ii).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.7: strong Zariski closedness is compatible with tilting
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. A map 𝒵 = Spa(S, S^+) → 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) is strongly Zariski closed if and only if the map of tilts 𝒵^♭ → 𝒳^♭ is strongly Zariski closed.
items.note: P4 node zariski-closed-tilting.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.8 (Kedlaya–Liu): surjections of perfectoid algebras are almost surjective on power-bounded elements
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. Let R → S be a surjective map of perfectoid K-algebras. Then R° → S° is almost surjective.
items.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.2.8, p. 957 (citing Kedlaya–Liu, Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations, Proposition 3.6.9(c))
items.note: P4 node surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.9(i): Zariski closed embeddings are stable under base change
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. Let 𝒵′ = Spa(S′, S′^+) → 𝒳′ = Spa(R′, R′^+) be the pullback of 𝒵 = Spa(S, S^+) → 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) along 𝒳′ → 𝒳, all affinoid perfectoid (fibre products exist by Perfectoid spaces, Proposition 6.18). If 𝒵 → 𝒳 is Zariski closed, defined by I ⊂ R, then 𝒵′ → 𝒳′ is Zariski closed, defined by IR′ ⊂ R′.
items.note: P4 node zariski-closed-base-change.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.9(ii): strongly Zariski closed embeddings are stable under base change, with almost surjective ideals
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K^♭, 0 ≠ ϖ^♭ ∈ K^♭ with |ϖ^♭| < 1, ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, and 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+) an affinoid perfectoid space over K. In the pullback situation of Lemma 2.2.9, if 𝒵 → 𝒳 is strongly Zariski closed then so is 𝒵′ → 𝒳′; moreover, with I^+ = ker(R^+ → S^+) and I′^+ = ker(R′^+ → S′^+), the map I^+/ϖ^n ⊗_{R^+/ϖ^n} R′^+/ϖ^n → I′^+/ϖ^n is almost surjective for all n ≥ 0.
items.note: P4 node zariski-closed-base-change.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.1: the stalks of 𝒪^+/t
items.statement: For any adic space 𝒳 over a nonarchimedean field and 0 ≠ t in its maximal ideal, the stalk of 𝒪_𝒳^+/t at a point x with completed residue field k(x) and valuation subring k(x)^+ ⊂ k(x) is k(x)^+/t; hence the stalk of (𝒪_𝒳^+/t)^a is 𝒪_{k(x)}^a/t.
items.note: P4 node stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.2: the general perfectoid Hebbarkeitssatz
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic p with maximal ideal 𝔪_K, 0 ≠ t ∈ 𝔪_K, (R, R^+) a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra, 𝒳 = Spa(R, R^+), I ⊂ R an ideal with I^+ = I ∩ R^+, and 𝒵 = V(I) ⊂ 𝒳. There is a natural isomorphism of almost 𝒪_K-modules Hom_{R^+}(I^{+1/p^∞}, R^+/t)^a ≅ H^0(𝒳 ∖ 𝒵, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t)^a, where I^{+1/p^∞} is the ideal generated by all p-power roots of elements of I^+. For any x ∈ 𝒳 ∖ 𝒵 it commutes with evaluation H^0(𝒳 ∖ 𝒵, 𝒪^+/t)^a → 𝒪_{k(x)}^a/t and Hom_{R^+}(I^{+1/p^∞}, R^+/t)^a → Hom_{𝒪_{k(x)}}(I_{k(x)}^{+1/p^∞}, 𝒪_{k(x)}/t)^a = 𝒪_{k(x)}^a/t. (Remark 2.3.3: global sections of (𝒪^+/t)^a are (R^+/t)^a, I_{k(x)}^{+1/p^∞} is almost 𝒪_{k(x)} off 𝒵, and this requirement determines the map.)
items.note: TC.0 plans 'the exact extension theorem needed for bounded functions across the chosen boundary', with its almost ideal retained.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.4: base change of the ideal of p-power roots
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid K-algebra (K perfectoid of characteristic p), I ⊂ R an ideal, R′ a perfectoid K-algebra with a map R → R′, and I′ = IR′. Then I^{+1/p^∞} ⊗_{R^+} R′^+ → I′^{+1/p^∞} is an almost isomorphism.
items.note: Used to show the Hebbarkeitssatz is local and passes to rational subsets.

items.name: Corollary 2.3.5: the Hebbarkeitssatz on Hasse-type domains under resolution of singularities
items.statement: Let A_0 be normal, integral and of finite type over 𝔽_p, 0 ≠ f ∈ A_0, K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), S = A_0^{1/p^∞} ⊗̂_{𝔽_p} K with S^+ = S° = A_0^{1/p^∞} ⊗̂_{𝔽_p} 𝒪_K, 𝒴 = Spa(S, S^+), 𝒳 = {y ∈ 𝒴 : |f(y)| ≥ |t|} with (R, R^+) = (𝒪_𝒴(𝒳), 𝒪_𝒴^+(𝒳)), 0 ≠ I_0 ⊂ A_0 an ideal, I = I_0R and 𝒵 = V(I) ⊂ 𝒳. Assume Spec A_0 admits a resolution of singularities, i.e. a proper birational map T → Spec A_0 with T smooth over 𝔽_p. Then H^0(𝒳, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t)^a → H^0(𝒳 ∖ 𝒵, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t)^a is an isomorphism of almost 𝒪_K-modules.
items.note: In the application Spec A_0 is an open of the Siegel minimal compactification mod p, f the Hasse invariant, I_0 the boundary ideal; the toroidal compactification (Faltings–Chai) supplies the resolution.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.6: almost reflexivity of perfections of normal rings
items.statement: Let A_0 be normal, integral and of finite type over 𝔽_p, such that Spec A_0 admits a resolution of singularities, and let 0 ≠ f, g ∈ A_0. Then the maps A_0^{1/p^∞} → Hom_{A_0^{1/p^∞}}(g^{1/p^∞}A_0^{1/p^∞}, A_0^{1/p^∞}) and A_0^{1/p^∞}/f → Hom_{A_0^{1/p^∞}}(g^{1/p^∞}A_0^{1/p^∞}, A_0^{1/p^∞}/f) are almost isomorphisms with respect to the ideal generated by all f^{1/p^m}, m ≥ 0. (Remark 2.3.7: the first map is an isomorphism and the second injective without resolution of singularities, which is only needed for almost surjectivity of the second.)
items.note: TC.0: the extension theorem keeps its normality and codimension hypotheses.

items.name: Definition 2.3.8: good triples
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field and 0 ≠ t ∈ K with |p| ≤ |t| < 1. A triple (𝒳, 𝒵, 𝒰) consisting of an affinoid perfectoid space 𝒳 over K, a closed subset 𝒵 ⊂ 𝒳 and a quasicompact open 𝒰 ⊂ 𝒳 ∖ 𝒵 is good if H^0(𝒳, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t)^a ≅ H^0(𝒳 ∖ 𝒵, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t)^a ↪ H^0(𝒰, 𝒪_𝒰^+/t)^a. The notion is independent of t and compatible with tilting, and for a good triple the displayed maps are an isomorphism and an injection for every t ∈ 𝒪_K, including t = 0 (bounded functions extend uniquely from 𝒳 ∖ 𝒵 to 𝒳).
items.locator: §2.3.3, Definition 2.3.8 and the paragraph after it, p. 966

items.name: Lemma 2.3.9: a base good triple
items.statement: Setting: K perfectoid of characteristic p; R_0 a reduced Tate K-algebra topologically of finite type, 𝒳_0 = Spa(R_0, R_0°), R its completed perfection, 𝒳 = Spa(R, R°); I_0 ⊂ R_0, I = I_0R, 𝒵_0 = V(I_0), 𝒵 = V(I); 𝒰_0 ⊂ 𝒳_0 ∖ 𝒵_0 quasicompact open with preimage 𝒰. Let A_0 be normal, of finite type over 𝔽_p, admitting a resolution of singularities; let R_0 = (A_0 ⊗̂_{𝔽_p} K)⟨u⟩/(uf − t) for some f ∈ A_0 which is not a zero-divisor, and I_0 = JR_0 for an ideal J ⊂ A_0 with V(J) ⊂ Spec A_0 of codimension ≥ 2; let 𝒰_0 = {x ∈ 𝒳_0 : |g(x)| = 1 for some g ∈ J}. If K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), the triple (𝒳, 𝒵, 𝒰) is good.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.10: good triples lift along finite normal covers étale off the boundary
items.statement: Setting: K perfectoid of characteristic p; R_0 a reduced Tate K-algebra topologically of finite type, 𝒳_0 = Spa(R_0, R_0°), R its completed perfection, 𝒳 = Spa(R, R°); I_0 ⊂ R_0, I = I_0R, 𝒵_0 = V(I_0), 𝒵 = V(I); 𝒰_0 ⊂ 𝒳_0 ∖ 𝒵_0 quasicompact open with preimage 𝒰. Assume (𝒳, 𝒵, 𝒰) is good, R_0 is normal and V(I_0) ⊂ Spec R_0 has codimension ≥ 2. Let R_0′ be a finite normal R_0-algebra, étale outside V(I_0), with no irreducible component of Spec R_0′ mapping into V(I_0); let I_0′ = I_0R_0′, 𝒰_0′ the preimage of 𝒰_0, and R′, I′, 𝒳′, 𝒵′, 𝒰′ the associated perfectoid objects. (i) There is a perfect trace pairing tr_{R_0′/R_0} : R_0′ ⊗_{R_0} R_0′ → R_0. (ii) It induces an almost perfect trace pairing R′° ⊗_{R°} R′° → R°. (iii) For every open 𝒱 ⊂ 𝒳 with preimage 𝒱′ ⊂ 𝒳′, the trace pairing induces H^0(𝒱′, 𝒪_{𝒳′}^+/t)^a ≅ Hom_{R°/t}(R′°/t, H^0(𝒱, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t))^a. (iv) The triple (𝒳′, 𝒵′, 𝒰′) is good. (v) If 𝒳′ → 𝒳 is surjective, then H^0(𝒳, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t) → H^0(𝒳′, 𝒪_{𝒳′}^+/t) ∩ H^0(𝒰, 𝒪_𝒳^+/t) is an almost isomorphism.
items.note: R3 constructs traces for finite locally free and finite étale maps; P3 (almost purity) gives the almost perfect pairing in (ii).

items.name: Lemma 2.3.11 and Corollary 2.3.12: good triples pass to inverse limits and to algebraic extensions of the base field
items.statement: Setting: K perfectoid of characteristic p; R_0 a reduced Tate K-algebra topologically of finite type, 𝒳_0 = Spa(R_0, R_0°), R its completed perfection, 𝒳 = Spa(R, R°); I_0 ⊂ R_0, I = I_0R, 𝒵_0 = V(I_0), 𝒵 = V(I); 𝒰_0 ⊂ 𝒳_0 ∖ 𝒵_0 quasicompact open with preimage 𝒰. Let R_0^{(i)}, i ∈ I, be a filtered inductive system as in Lemma 2.3.10, giving 𝒳^{(i)}, 𝒵^{(i)}, 𝒰^{(i)}, with all transition maps 𝒳^{(i)} → 𝒳^{(j)} surjective; let 𝒳̃ be the inverse limit of the 𝒳^{(i)} in perfectoid spaces over K, and 𝒵̃, 𝒰̃ the preimages of 𝒵, 𝒰. Then (𝒳̃, 𝒵̃, 𝒰̃) is good (Lemma 2.3.11). Consequently the conclusion of Lemma 2.3.9 holds whenever K is the completion of an algebraic extension of 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) (Corollary 2.3.12).
items.note: P5 constructs the cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces used here.

items.name: Definition 3.1.1: the level subgroups Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m) of GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p)
items.statement: With g × g blocks: Γ_0(p^m) = {γ ∈ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p) : γ ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 ∗) mod p^m, det γ ≡ 1 mod p^m}; Γ_1(p^m) = {γ ∈ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p) : γ ≡ (1 ∗; 0 1) mod p^m}; Γ(p^m) = {γ ∈ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p) : γ ≡ 1 mod p^m}. (The condition det γ ≡ 1 in Γ_0(p^m) is nonstandard.) X*_{Γ_0(p^m)} lives naturally over ℚ(ζ_{p^m}) through the similitude factor.
items.locator: §3.1, Definition 3.1.1 and the remarks after it, p. 971
items.note: S0 constructs the p-level inverse systems and their cofinal congruence systems with the group actions.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.1 (Illusie): obstruction theory for lifting morphisms of flat commutative group schemes
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, G, H flat and finitely presented commutative group schemes over A, and u : H → G a group morphism. Let B_1, B_2 → A be square-zero thickenings with a morphism B_1 → B_2 over A, J_i ⊂ B_i the augmentation ideals, G̃_1 a lift of G to B_1 and G̃_2 the induced lift to B_2, and K a cone of the map ℓ̌_H → ℓ̌_G of co-Lie complexes. (i) For i = 1, 2 there is an obstruction class o_i ∈ Ext^1(H, K ⊗^𝕃 J_i) which vanishes exactly when there is a lifting (H̃_i, ũ_i) of (H, u) to a flat commutative group scheme H̃_i over B_i with a morphism ũ_i : H̃_i → G̃_i lifting u. (ii) o_2 is the image of o_1 under the map induced by J_1 → J_2.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Theorem 3.2.1, p. 975 (citing Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations II, and Illusie's Oberwolfach report)
items.note: Missing: no atlas layer plans Illusie's deformation theory of flat commutative group schemes via Lie complexes. DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 plans cotangent complexes of rings, and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.6 the tangent and obstruction calculations for finite flat groups; routed as a source of R07.6. Remark 3.2.3 notes that the canonical-subgroup application can instead use the deformation theory of rings (Illusie I), at the cost of larger explicit constants.

items.name: Corollary 3.2.2: lifting a subgroup modulo p to a finite locally free subgroup, with explicit error
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra, G a finite locally free commutative group scheme over R, and C_1 ⊂ G ⊗_R R/p a finite locally free subgroup. Assume that for H = (G ⊗_R R/p)/C_1, multiplication by p^ε on the co-Lie complex ℓ̌_H is homotopic to 0, where 0 ≤ ε < 1/2. Then there is a finite locally free subgroup C ⊂ G over R with C ⊗_R R/p^{1−ε} = C_1 ⊗_{R/p} R/p^{1−ε}.
items.note: Missing: T3 plans existence of canonical subgroups with quantitative bounds but no lifting lemma of this form; routed as a source of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T3. Remark 3.2.3 gives the alternative through deformation of rings (lift H, then its multiplication and inverse, then G ⊗ R/p → H), with errors p^{1−2ε} and p^{1−3ε}.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.4: sections agreeing to high order are equal when Ω^1 is killed by p^ε
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra and X/R a scheme such that Ω^1_{X/R} is killed by p^ε for some ε ≥ 0. Let s, t ∈ X(R) be sections with s̄ = t̄ in X(R/p^δ) for some δ > ε. Then s = t.
items.note: T3 plans the integral differential estimates behind uniqueness of canonical subgroups.

items.name: The Hasse invariant of an abelian scheme in characteristic p, Lemma 3.2.5, and its extension to the minimal compactification
items.statement: Let S be a scheme of characteristic p and A → S an abelian scheme of dimension g, with A^{(p)} its Frobenius pullback. The Verschiebung V : A^{(p)} → A induces V* : ω_{A/S} → ω_{A^{(p)}/S} ≅ ω_{A/S}^{⊗p}, i.e. a section Ha(A/S) ∈ ω_{A/S}^{⊗(p−1)} (ω the determinant of the invariant differentials), the Hasse invariant. Lemma 3.2.5: Ha(A/S) is invertible if and only if A is ordinary, i.e. A[p](x̄) has p^g elements for every geometric point x̄ of S. On the Siegel moduli space, Ha ∈ H^0(X_{𝔽_p}, ω^{⊗(p−1)}) extends to Ha ∈ H^0(X*_{𝔽_p}, ω^{⊗(p−1)}): for g ≥ 2 by the classical Hartogs principle (the boundary of X* has codimension g), for g = 1 by direct inspection.
items.locator: §3.2.1, the paragraph before Lemma 3.2.5 and Lemma 3.2.5, p. 977; §3.2.2, p. 983
items.note: Missing for the Siegel moduli space: AdicSpacesPartII R2's hasse-domain node takes Ha as input 'supplied by the moduli roadmaps', and the atlas constructs it only for modular curves (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.3), Hilbert varieties (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2, ShimuraCompactifications C6) and the unitary Ekedahl–Oort strata of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2. Routed as a source of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T3, whose Siegel canonical subgroups need it.

items.name: Corollary 3.2.6 (with Lemma 3.1.3): canonical subgroups on Hasse neighbourhoods and their integral points
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra and A → Spec R an abelian scheme with reduction A_1 → Spec R/p. Assume Ha(A_1/Spec(R/p))^{(p^m−1)/(p−1)} divides p^ε for some ε < 1/2. Then there is a unique closed subgroup C_m ⊂ A[p^m], flat over R, with C_m = Ker F^m ⊂ A[p^m] modulo p^{1−ε}. For any p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra R′ with a map R → R′, C_m(R′) = {s ∈ A[p^m](R′) : s ≡ 0 mod p^{(1−ε)/p^m}}. (Lemma 3.1.3 is the same existence and uniqueness statement for an abelian variety over such an R.)
items.note: T3: existence, uniqueness and base change of canonical subgroups, and the reduction-to-iterated-Frobenius characterization.

items.name: Definition 3.2.7: weak and strong canonical subgroups of level m
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra. An abelian scheme A → Spec R has a weak canonical subgroup of level m if Ha(A_1/Spec(R/p))^{(p^m−1)/(p−1)} divides p^ε for some ε < 1/2; then the weak canonical subgroup of level m is the unique closed subgroup C_m ⊂ A[p^m] with C_m = Ker F^m mod p^{1−ε}. If moreover Ha(A_1/Spec(R/p))^{p^m} divides p^ε, C_m is called a (strong) canonical subgroup.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.8(i)–(ii): canonical subgroups of smaller level and functoriality
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra and A, B → Spec R abelian schemes. (i) If A has a canonical subgroup C_m ⊂ A[p^m] of level m, then it has a canonical subgroup C_{m′} ⊂ A[p^{m′}] of every level m′ ≤ m, and C_{m′} ⊂ C_m. (ii) If f : A → B is a morphism of abelian schemes and A, B have canonical subgroups C_m ⊂ A[p^m], D_m ⊂ B[p^m] of level m, then f maps C_m into D_m.
items.note: T3: isogeny compatibility and base change.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.8(iii): canonical subgroups of the quotient by a canonical subgroup
items.statement: Let A → Spec R (R a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra) have a canonical subgroup C_{m_1} ⊂ A[p^{m_1}] of level m_1. Then B = A/C_{m_1} has a canonical subgroup D_{m_2} ⊂ B[p^{m_2}] of level m_2 if and only if A has a canonical subgroup C_m ⊂ A[p^m] of level m = m_1 + m_2; in that case there is a short exact sequence 0 → C_{m_1} → C_m → D_{m_2} → 0 compatible with 0 → C_{m_1} → A → B → 0.
items.note: T3: 'the effect of division by the canonical subgroup on the Hasse radius'.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.8(iv): geometric generic points of a canonical subgroup
items.statement: If A → Spec R has a canonical subgroup C_m ⊂ A[p^m] of level m and x̄ is a geometric point of Spec R[p^{-1}], then C_m(x̄) ≅ (ℤ/p^mℤ)^g, where g is the dimension of the abelian variety over x̄.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.9 and Lemma 3.2.10: algebraic and formal Hartogs extension
items.statement: Proposition 3.2.9: for R normal and noetherian and Z ⊂ Spec R everywhere of codimension ≥ 2, R = H^0(Spec R ∖ Z, 𝒪_{Spec R}). Lemma 3.2.10: let R be a topologically finitely generated flat p-adically complete ℤ_p-algebra with R̄ = R/p normal, f ∈ R with f̄ not a zero divisor in R̄, 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1, and S = (R ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p^cycl)⟨u⟩/(fu − p^ε). Then S is a flat p-adically complete ℤ_p^cycl-algebra and u is not a zero divisor; for a closed Y ⊂ Spec R̄ of codimension ≥ 2 with preimage Z ⊂ Spf S and complement U, H^0(U, 𝒪_{Spf S}) = H^0(Spf S, 𝒪_{Spf S}) = S. (Remark 3.2.11 compares this with Hartogs' theorem over ℂ.)
items.note: TC.0 plans the extension theorem with its codimension and normality hypotheses; R2's node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-extension is the Bosch–Lütkebohmert form.

items.name: Definition 3.2.12 and Lemma 3.2.13 as corrected: the Hasse domains 𝔛*(ε) and their local equations
items.statement: Setting of §3: X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure, K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in the level-N congruence subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p; X* is its minimal compactification (Faltings–Chai) with ample ω; ℚ_p^cycl is the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); 𝔛, 𝔛* are the p-adic completions of X, X* over ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒳, 𝒳* their generic fibres, 𝒜 → 𝒳 the universal abelian variety; for K_p ∈ {Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m)} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p), 𝒳*_{K_p} is the adic space over ℚ_p^cycl of X*_{K_pK^p} and 𝒳_{K_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_p} the preimage of 𝒳 (the locus of good reduction); ~ is the tilde-limit of Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 2.4.1. Let 0 ≤ ε < 1 with an element p^ε ∈ ℤ_p^cycl of valuation ε. 𝔛*(ε) → 𝔛* over Spf ℤ_p^cycl is the functor sending a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p^cycl-algebra S to pairs (f, u), f : Spf S → 𝔛* and u ∈ H^0(Spf S, f*ω^{⊗(1−p)}) with u·Ha(f̄) = p^ε in S/p, up to (f, u) ~ (f, u(1 + p^{1−ε}h)), h ∈ S. Lemma 3.2.13: 𝔛*(ε) is representable by a formal scheme flat over ℤ_p^cycl; over an affine Spf(R ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p^cycl) ⊂ 𝔛* coming from Spf R ⊂ 𝔛*_{ℤ_p}, with a lift H̃a ∈ ω^{⊗(p−1)} of Ha, 𝔛*(ε) ×_{𝔛*} Spf(R ⊗̂ ℤ_p^cycl) = Spf((R ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p^cycl)⟨u⟩/(uH̃a − p^ε)). Consequently 𝔛*(ε) → 𝔛* is an open formal subscheme of an admissible blow-up (the chart of the blow-up of (H̃a, p^ε) on which H̃a generates), not itself an admissible blow-up (sourceIssues E3). By pullback one has 𝔛(ε), 𝔄(ε), and on generic fibres 𝒳*(ε) = {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε}.
items.locator: §3.2.2, Definition 3.2.12, Lemma 3.2.13 and the paragraph after it, pp. 983–984

items.name: Lemma 3.2.14: the Frobenius diagram modulo p on Hasse domains
items.statement: Setting of §3: X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure, K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in the level-N congruence subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p; X* is its minimal compactification (Faltings–Chai) with ample ω; ℚ_p^cycl is the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); 𝔛, 𝔛* are the p-adic completions of X, X* over ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒳, 𝒳* their generic fibres, 𝒜 → 𝒳 the universal abelian variety; for K_p ∈ {Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m)} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p), 𝒳*_{K_p} is the adic space over ℚ_p^cycl of X*_{K_pK^p} and 𝒳_{K_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_p} the preimage of 𝒳 (the locus of good reduction); ~ is the tilde-limit of Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 2.4.1. Let 0 ≤ ε < 1. The relative Frobenius maps F of 𝔄(p^{-1}ε)/p, 𝔛(p^{-1}ε)/p and 𝔛*(p^{-1}ε)/p over ℤ_p^cycl/p, followed by the isomorphisms (𝔜(p^{-1}ε)/p)^{(p)} ≅ 𝔜(ε)/p, form a natural commutative diagram 𝔄(p^{-1}ε)/p → 𝔄(ε)/p over 𝔛(p^{-1}ε)/p → 𝔛(ε)/p over 𝔛*(p^{-1}ε)/p → 𝔛*(ε)/p.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.15(i): canonical Frobenius lifts on Hasse domains
items.statement: Setting of §3: X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure, K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in the level-N congruence subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p; X* is its minimal compactification (Faltings–Chai) with ample ω; ℚ_p^cycl is the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); 𝔛, 𝔛* are the p-adic completions of X, X* over ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒳, 𝒳* their generic fibres, 𝒜 → 𝒳 the universal abelian variety; for K_p ∈ {Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m)} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p), 𝒳*_{K_p} is the adic space over ℚ_p^cycl of X*_{K_pK^p} and 𝒳_{K_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_p} the preimage of 𝒳 (the locus of good reduction); ~ is the tilde-limit of Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 2.4.1. Let 0 ≤ ε < 1/2. There is a unique diagram of formal schemes F̃ : 𝔄(p^{-1}ε) → 𝔄(ε), 𝔛(p^{-1}ε) → 𝔛(ε), 𝔛*(p^{-1}ε) → 𝔛*(ε), compatible with the projections, which is identified with the diagram of Lemma 3.2.14 modulo p^{1−ε}. (F̃_𝔛 sends A to A/C with C the canonical subgroup of level 1.) These maps are finite locally free, F̃_𝔛 of degree p^{g(g+1)/2} (sourceIssues E4).
items.note: S1: 'integral transition maps approximate Frobenius with the required estimates'.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.15(ii): the anticanonical open immersions 𝒳*(p^{−m}ε) → 𝒳*_{Γ_0(p^m)}
items.statement: Setting of §3: X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure, K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in the level-N congruence subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p; X* is its minimal compactification (Faltings–Chai) with ample ω; ℚ_p^cycl is the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); 𝔛, 𝔛* are the p-adic completions of X, X* over ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒳, 𝒳* their generic fibres, 𝒜 → 𝒳 the universal abelian variety; for K_p ∈ {Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m)} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p), 𝒳*_{K_p} is the adic space over ℚ_p^cycl of X*_{K_pK^p} and 𝒳_{K_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_p} the preimage of 𝒳 (the locus of good reduction); ~ is the tilde-limit of Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 2.4.1. Let 0 ≤ ε < 1/2. For any m ≥ 0, 𝔄(p^{−m}ε) → 𝔛(p^{−m}ε) admits a canonical subgroup C_m ⊂ 𝔄(p^{−m}ε)[p^m] of level m. The pair (𝒜(p^{−m}ε)/C_m, 𝒜(p^{−m}ε)[p^m]/C_m) defines a morphism 𝒳(p^{−m}ε) → 𝒳_{Γ_0(p^m)} on generic fibres, which extends uniquely to 𝒳*(p^{−m}ε) → 𝒳*_{Γ_0(p^m)}; these morphisms are open immersions. For m ≥ 1 the square with top 𝒳*(p^{−m−1}ε) → 𝒳*_{Γ_0(p^{m+1})}, left (F̃_{𝔛(p^{−m−1}ε)})^ad_η, right the forgetful map and bottom 𝒳*(p^{−m}ε) → 𝒳*_{Γ_0(p^m)} is commutative and cartesian.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.15(iii) as corrected, and Remark 3.2.16: the anticanonical locus at level Γ_0(p)
items.statement: Setting of §3: X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure, K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in the level-N congruence subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p; X* is its minimal compactification (Faltings–Chai) with ample ω; ℚ_p^cycl is the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); 𝔛, 𝔛* are the p-adic completions of X, X* over ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒳, 𝒳* their generic fibres, 𝒜 → 𝒳 the universal abelian variety; for K_p ∈ {Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m)} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p), 𝒳*_{K_p} is the adic space over ℚ_p^cycl of X*_{K_pK^p} and 𝒳_{K_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_p} the preimage of 𝒳 (the locus of good reduction); ~ is the tilde-limit of Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 2.4.1. Let 0 ≤ ε < 1/2. There is a weak canonical subgroup C ⊂ 𝔄(ε)[p] of level 1 (printed: 'of level p'; sourceIssues E5); write also C ⊂ 𝒜(ε)[p] for its generic fibre, and let 𝒳_{Γ_0(p)}(ε) → 𝒳(ε) be the pullback of 𝒳_{Γ_0(p)} → 𝒳. items.name: Lemma 3.2.21: trace estimates for Frobenius-type finite free extensions
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p-algebra, Y_1, …, Y_n ∈ R, and P_1, …, P_n ∈ R⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ topologically nilpotent; let S = R⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩/(X_1^p − Y_1 − P_1, …, X_n^p − Y_n − P_n). (i) S is a finite free R-module with basis X_1^{i_1}⋯X_n^{i_n}, 0 ≤ i_1, …, i_n ≤ p − 1. (ii) If I_i ⊂ R is the ideal generated by the coefficients of P_i and I = (p, I_1, …, I_n), then tr_{S/R}(S) ⊂ I^n.
items.note: R3 constructs traces of finite locally free algebras.

items.name: Corollary 3.2.22: the trace of a Frobenius lift on Hasse domains is divisible by p^{n−(2n+1)ε}
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete ℤ_p-algebra topologically of finite type, formally smooth of dimension n, and f ∈ R with f̄ ∈ R/p not a zero divisor. For 0 ≤ ε < 1 let R_ε = (R ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p^cycl)⟨u_ε⟩/(fu_ε − p^ε). Let φ : R_ε → R_{ε/p} be a map of ℤ_p^cycl-algebras which modulo p^{1−ε} is the map (R̄ ⊗_{𝔽_p} ℤ_p^cycl/p^{1−ε})[u_ε]/(fu_ε − p^ε) → (R̄ ⊗ ℤ_p^cycl/p^{1−ε})[u_{ε/p}]/(fu_{ε/p} − p^{ε/p}) given by Frobenius on R̄ and u_ε ↦ u_{ε/p}^p; assume ε < 1/2. (i) φ[1/p] : R_ε[1/p] → R_{ε/p}[1/p] is finite and flat. (ii) The trace tr : R_{ε/p}[1/p] → R_ε[1/p] maps R_{ε/p} into p^{n−(2n+1)ε}R_ε.

items.name: The flag variety Fl, its line bundle ω_Fl and the affinoids Fl_J
items.statement: Fl over ℚ is the flag variety of totally isotropic g-dimensional subspaces W ⊂ V of the symplectic space (V, ψ) of dimension 2g, with tautological ample line bundle ω_Fl = (∧^g W)*; also the associated adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). Via the Plücker embedding Fl ↪ ℙ^{C(2g,g)−1}, for J ⊂ {1, …, 2g} of cardinality g with homogeneous coordinate s_J, Fl_J ⊂ Fl is the open affinoid where |s_{J′}| ≤ |s_J| for all J′. GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p) permutes the Fl_J transitively; Fl_{g+1,…,2g}(ℚ_p) ⊂ Fl(ℚ_p) = Fl(ℤ_p) parametrizes the totally isotropic direct summands M ⊂ ℤ_p^{2g} with M ⊕ (ℤ_p^g ⊕ 0^g) ≅ ℤ_p^{2g}.
items.locator: §3.1, p. 971; §3.3, the paragraph before Lemma 3.3.8, p. 1008

items.name: Proposition 3.3.1: the Hodge–Tate filtration of an abelian variety and of the p-divisible group of its Néron model
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete extension of ℚ_p, A/C an abelian variety with connected Néron model G/𝒪_C, and Ĝ its p-adic completion. For any tame level K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in {γ ∈ GSp_{2g}(ℤ̂^p) : γ ≡ 1 mod N} for some N ≥ 3 prime to p there is a perfectoid space 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} over ℚ_p^cycl, unique up to unique isomorphism, with 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} ~ lim_m 𝒳*_{Γ(p^m),K^p} and a GSp_{2g}(ℚ_p)-action, and a GSp_{2g}(ℚ_p)-equivariant Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} → Fl of adic spaces over ℚ_p. (iii) For (K^p)′ ⊂ K^p, π_HT on 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),(K^p)′} factors through the projection to 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p}. (iv) For γ ∈ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) with γ^{-1}K^pγ in a level-N subgroup (N ≥ 3 prime to p), π_HT ∘ γ = π_HT : 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} → 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),γ^{-1}K^pγ} → Fl; thus π_HT commutes with the Hecke operators away from p for the trivial action on Fl.
items.note: PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S1 is 'The Siegel construction' of exactly this theorem.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.18(v)–(vi): Lie A and ω as pullbacks along the Hodge–Tate period map
items.statement: Setting of §3: X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure, K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) contained in the level-N congruence subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p; X* is its minimal compactification (Faltings–Chai) with ample ω; ℚ_p^cycl is the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); 𝔛, 𝔛* are the p-adic completions of X, X* over ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒳, 𝒳* their generic fibres, 𝒜 → 𝒳 the universal abelian variety; for K_p ∈ {Γ_0(p^m), Γ_1(p^m), Γ(p^m)} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p), 𝒳*_{K_p} is the adic space over ℚ_p^cycl of X*_{K_pK^p} and 𝒳_{K_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_p} the preimage of 𝒳 (the locus of good reduction); ~ is the tilde-limit of Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 2.4.1. (v) Let W_Fl ⊂ 𝒪_Fl^{2g} be the universal totally isotropic subspace. Over 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} ∖ 𝒵_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} there is a natural GSp_{2g}(ℚ_p)-equivariant isomorphism Lie A_{K^p} ≅ π_HT*W_Fl (Lie A_{K^p} the Lie algebra of the tautological abelian variety), with the analogues of (iii) and (iv). (vi) With ω_Fl = (∧^g W_Fl)* and ω_{K^p} the natural line bundle on 𝒳*_{Γ(p^∞),K^p} (pulled back from any finite level), there is a natural GSp_{2g}(ℚ_p)-equivariant isomorphism ω_{K^p} ≅ π_HT*ω_Fl extending the isomorphism from (v), with the analogues of (iii) and (iv).
items.note: The proof of (vi) bounds the isomorphism integrally (p^C ω^+ ⊂ π_HT*ω_Fl^+ ⊂ p^{−C} ω^+, via Fargues' Théorème II.1.1 or induction on g) and extends it by the Hebbarkeitssatz; TC.1 plans the integral comparison of automorphic bundle lattices with pullbacks along π_HT.

items.name: The Hodge-type setting of §4: X_K, X*_K, the normalization-free image X_K** and the bundle ω_K
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. There are natural finite maps X_K → Y_{K′} and X*_K → Y*_{K′} to the Siegel varieties for G′ = Sp_{2g}; for every K there is K′ with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) and X_K → Y_{K′} a closed embedding (Deligne, Travaux de Shimura, Proposition 1.15), whereas for the minimal compactification this is not known, which is why X_K** is used. G(𝔸_f) acts on the tower (X_K**)_K, and H^0(X*_K, ω_K^{⊗k}) consists of complex automorphic forms.
items.note: S2: 'Choose a symplectic embedding, compare finite-level varieties with their Siegel images'.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.1 (with Theorems 1.0.6 and 1.0.8): perfectoid Shimura varieties of Hodge type and their Hodge–Tate period map
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. Remark 5.4.6 uses that the theorem holds verbatim for Shimura varieties of Hodge type in the usual sense (unitary similitude groups).

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1 (with Theorem 1.0.5): Hecke eigenvalues in completed cohomology are interpolated by classical cusp forms
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. Let 𝕋 be the abstract Hecke algebra away from p acting on the H^i_c(X_{K_pK^p}) and on cusp forms. items.name: Lemma 4.3.2: traces of finite generically étale extensions of normal rings are integral
items.statement: Let R be normal and S a finite, generically étale R-algebra, i.e. S[f^{-1}] is finite étale over R[f^{-1}] for some non-zero-divisor f ∈ R. Then tr_{S[f^{-1}]/R[f^{-1}]} : S[f^{-1}] → R[f^{-1}] maps S into R. Moreover, for any integrally closed ideal I ⊂ R with integral closure J ⊂ S, tr(J) ⊂ I.
items.note: R3 constructs traces of finite locally free and finite étale maps; TC.2 needs them for the Hecke trace maps on completed cohomology.

items.name: Proposition 5.1.1: holomorphic discrete series of Sp_{2n}(ℝ) and U(n,n) with scalar minimal K-type
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = Sp_{2n}/ℝ, resp. U(n,n)/ℝ, with maximal compact K ⊂ 𝒢(ℝ), standard Borel ℬ with torus 𝒯, X*(𝒯_ℂ) = ℤ^n resp. ℤ^{2n}. items.name: Theorem 5.1.4: Galois representations for regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations
items.statement: Let F be totally real or CM and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n with (Π^∨)^c ≅ Π and Π|·|^{k/2} regular L-algebraic for some integer k. items.name: Lemma 5.1.6(i): the unramified Hecke algebra of Sp_{2n} and the transfer to GL_{2n+1}

items.name: Lemma 5.1.6(ii)–(iii): the unramified Hecke algebra of the quasisplit unitary group at split and inert places

items.name: Definition 5.1.8 and Remark 5.1.9: determinants, their (nonstandard) characteristic polynomials and continuity
items.statement: Let A be a (topological) ring and G a (topological) group. A d-dimensional determinant is an A-polynomial law D : A[G] → A which is multiplicative and homogeneous of degree d; for g ∈ G, D(1 − Xg) ∈ A[X] is the characteristic polynomial of g, and D is continuous if g ↦ D(1 − Xg), G → A[X], is continuous (Chenevier, 2.30). More generally, for an A-algebra B a multiplicative A-polynomial law A[G] → B homogeneous of degree d is a determinant of dimension d with values in B; equivalently a multiplicative B-polynomial law B[G] → B homogeneous of degree d.
items.note: IHG.0 packet nodes determinant, characteristic-polynomial, continuous-determinant and determinant-base-change (from Chenevier's paper).

items.name: Corollary 5.1.11: determinants over discrete continuous quotients of the classical Hecke algebra

items.name: The Borel–Serre boundary, its long exact sequence and the parabolic stratum

items.name: The Hecke algebras 𝕋_{K^{S^+}}, 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}}, 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}}, the unnormalized Satake transform and their actions on boundary cohomology
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. items.name: Lemma 5.3.10: uniqueness of the decomposition of a power series by T-weight
items.statement: Let S be a commutative ring and Q ∈ S[T^{±1}][[X]] with Q ≡ 1 mod X. There is at most one way to write Q = ∏_{m∈ℤ} Q_m with Q_m ∈ S[[XT^m]], Q_m ≡ 1 mod X, almost all equal to 1. If Q ∈ S[T^{±1}][X], then all Q_m ∈ S[XT^m].

items.name: Lemmas 5.3.11–5.3.12: the multiplicative maps D_0^{(m)}
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 5.3.8: (5.3.11) for any R-algebra S there are unique multiplicative maps D_0^{(m)} : 1 + US[G][[U]] → 1 + US[[U]] with D̃(f(XV)) = ∏_{m∈ℤ} D_0^{(m)}(f(XT^m)) in S[T^{±1}][[X]] for all f(U) ∈ 1 + US[G][[U]]; they satisfy D_0^{(m)}(1 − U^axg) = P_g^{(m)}(U^ax) for a ≥ 1, x ∈ S, g ∈ G, and map 1 + US[G][U] into 1 + US[U]. (5.3.12) For a nilpotent ideal I ⊂ S and f ∈ 1 + US[G][U] with f ≡ 1 mod I and f|_{U=1} = 1, D_0^{(m)}(f)|_{U=1} = 1.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.13: multiplicative polynomial laws decompose into homogeneous ones
items.statement: Let R[G] → R be a multiplicative R-polynomial law. Then for some integer N there is a decomposition R = R_0 × ⋯ × R_N × R_∞ into direct factors such that for 0 ≤ d ≤ N the induced multiplicative R_d-polynomial law R_d[G] → R_d is homogeneous of degree d (a determinant of dimension d), and R_∞[G] → R_∞ is constantly 0.
items.note: IHG.0 plans homogeneous and multiplicative polynomial laws (Roby, Chenevier); the decomposition by degree is part of that theory as used in TC.3's factor extraction.

items.name: The coefficient systems ℳ_{ξ,K} and the Hecke algebras 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m)
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Fix an algebraic representation ξ of Res_{𝒪_F/ℤ}GL_n on a finite free ℤ_p-module M_ξ (coefficients later extended to ℤ̄_p); it defines a local system ℳ_{ξ,K} of ℤ_p-modules on X_K for every K. By the Satake isomorphism 𝕋_v[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n}, and q_v^{i(n+1)/2}T_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_v. 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ̄_p/p^m}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}/p^m))).
items.note: ALS.1: local systems from algebraic representations with stable lattices.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.1: Galois determinants for torsion in the cohomology of GL_n over totally real and CM fields
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. There is an integer N = N([F:ℚ], n), depending only on [F:ℚ] and n, such that for any compact open K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) as above, any algebraic representation ξ and any integers i, m ≥ 0: there is an ideal I ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m) with I^N = 0 and an n-dimensional continuous determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m)/I satisfying D(1 − X Frob_v) = P_v(X) for all v ∉ S.
items.note: The main theorem. Following the accepted extractions PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/72, PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23/thm-2-1-24 and PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-24/2, which cite it, it is planned by TC.2–TC.4 with IHG.5's nilpotent descent. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure's summary says formalizing this final theorem is 'not an additional requirement'; that is a scope statement about the roadmap's target, while TC.4's contract (§5.4: 'compatibility checks and reusable specialization infrastructure') and IHG.5 plan exactly its assembly. Proof: Hochschild–Serre along a normal K′ ⊂ K on which ℳ_{ξ,K′}/p^m is trivial reduces to K small and ξ trivial; the Borel–Serre sequence splits the Hecke action into the interior part (Theorem 5.3.1) and the boundary part, which is expressed through the locally symmetric spaces of GL_{n′}, n′ < n, and handled by induction (left in the paper as 'an easy exercise', citing Caraiani–Le Hung §3, so the TC.3 design has to write it out); the two are glued along a square-zero kernel by Chenevier, Corollary 1.14. The totally real case assumes Arthur (ML.4); see Remark 5.4.6.

items.name: Corollary 5.4.2 (= Theorem 1.0.4): Galois representations for regular L-algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n
items.statement: Let F be totally real or CM and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with π_∞ regular L-algebraic and π_v unramified at all finite v ∉ S. Then there is a unique continuous semisimple σ_π : G_{F,S} → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) such that for all finite v ∉ S the Satake parameters of π_v agree with the eigenvalues of σ_π(Frob_v).
items.note: The theorem of Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, which Scholze reproves via Theorem 5.4.1; AG2.4 plans the HLTT route (its text says it 'does not use Scholze's torsion Hecke interpolation'), so the statement is planned but not this proof.

items.name: Corollary 5.4.3 (the precise form of Theorem 1.0.3): mod p Galois representations for Hecke eigensystems in torsion cohomology
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Let ψ : 𝕋_{F,S} → 𝔽̄_p be a system of Hecke eigenvalues with H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K} ⊗_{ℤ̄_p} 𝔽̄_p)[ψ] ≠ 0. Then there is a unique continuous semisimple σ_ψ : G_{F,S} → GL_n(𝔽̄_p) with det(1 − X Frob_v | σ_ψ) = 1 − ψ(q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v})X + ψ(q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v})X² − ⋯ + (−1)^nψ(q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v})X^n for all finite v ∉ S.
items.note: As PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/69: the determinant specializes to 𝔽̄_p (IHG.5) and a determinant over an algebraically closed field comes from a unique semisimple representation (IHG.1).

items.name: Corollary 5.4.4 as corrected: Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations for non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Let ψ be as in Corollary 5.4.3 with σ_ψ irreducible, 𝔪 = ker ψ ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}, 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ̄_p}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}))), and N = N([F:ℚ], n) as in Theorem 5.4.1. Then there is an ideal I ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i) with I^N = 0 and a unique continuous representation σ_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i)_𝔪/I) such that for all finite v ∉ S, det(1 − X Frob_v | σ_𝔪) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n (printed with σ_ψ on the left; sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Remark 5.4.5: the Calegari–Geraghty existence statement (Conjecture B, modulo a nilpotent ideal)
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Corollary 5.4.4 holds, with the same proof, with 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i) replaced by 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i)′ = im(𝕋_{F,S} → ⊕_m End_{ℤ̄_p/p^m}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}/p^m))) or by 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → ⊕_{i,m} End_{ℤ̄_p/p^m}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}/p^m))). This gives the Galois representations of Calegari–Geraghty's Conjecture B up to a nilpotent ideal of bounded nilpotence degree, without their expected local properties.
items.note: IHG.2: Hecke algebras acting on all degrees of a bounded complex. The local properties of Conjecture B are not claimed.

items.name: Remark 5.4.6: the unconditional range
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. The results of §5 rest on Arthur (resp. Mok), conditional on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula. By Shin's results (Goldring's appendix; cf. Morel, Corollary 8.5.3) all results of §5 are unconditional if (i) F is CM and contains an imaginary-quadratic field, and (ii) S is the pullback of a finite set S_ℚ of finite places of ℚ containing p and the places where F/ℚ ramifies; in particular for F imaginary quadratic they hold as stated. Theorem 4.1.1 and Chapter 4 hold verbatim for Shimura varieties of Hodge type attached to unitary similitude groups, so the argument of Chapter 5 applies to them. By a patching argument (Harris–Taylor, Theorem VII.1.9) Corollary 5.4.2 follows for general totally real or CM F, still assuming S comes from a set S_ℚ containing the places where F/ℚ ramifies.

routes.reason: R07.6 plans 'the deformation-theoretic tangent and obstruction calculations' for finite flat and p-divisible groups and already depends on DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0–DD.1 for cotangent complexes. Illusie's obstruction class o ∈ Ext^1(H, K ⊗^𝕃 J) for lifting a morphism u : H → G of flat, finitely presented commutative group schemes along a square-zero thickening, with its functoriality in the thickening (Theorem 3.2.1), is exactly such a calculation, one level more general than p-divisible groups. It belongs inside that layer, not in a new roadmap; the only consumer here is the canonical-subgroup lifting lemma routed to T3, and Remark 3.2.3 shows T3 could instead use DD.0's deformation theory of rings with worse constants.

T3 plans canonical subgroups with quantitative bounds on Hasse neighbourhoods, and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S1 ('The Siegel construction') consumes T3–T4 for the Siegel tower; but T3's text is written for the Hilbert application of BHW and takes its Hasse neighbourhoods from AdicSpacesPartII R2, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2 and ShimuraCompactifications C6, none of which constructs the Hasse invariant of a g-dimensional abelian scheme. Scholze §3.2.1 is the source for the Siegel case: the Hasse invariant Ha(A/S) from Verschiebung, Lemma 3.2.5 (invertible exactly on the ordinary locus) and its extension to the minimal compactification, the lifting lemma Corollary 3.2.2 (with Remark 3.2.3's elementary alternative), and Lemma 3.3.2 on Ha at boundary points, which are missing; and Lemma 3.2.4, Corollary 3.2.6, Definition 3.2.7 and Proposition 3.2.8, which T3 plans, with the explicit constants ε < 1/2 and p^{1−ε}. Theorem 3.2.15 (Frobenius lifts and the anticanonical open immersions, T3/T4), Proposition 3.3.1 (Hodge–Tate filtration through the Raynaud extension, T0) and Lemma 3.3.4 (the period map on points, T2) are planned items for which the paper is the natural source.

AF.4 defines infinitesimal characters and cohomological representations and AF.5 proves the dictionary between automorphic representations and classical modular forms for GL_1 and GL_2/ℚ. §5.1 needs the next case of both: the unique discrete series π_k of Sp_{2n}(ℝ) or U(n,n) with minimal K-type χ^k and its infinitesimal character (Proposition 5.1.1), and the identification of the Hecke eigensystems in weight-k holomorphic cusp forms H^0(X*_K, ω^k ⊗ ℐ) with cuspidal π having π_∞ ≅ π_k, semisimple by the Petersson product. These are extensions inside those layers' direction, not a new roadmap; ET.1's unitary pseudocoefficients do not cover the symplectic case.
